claims.claim: A case must pass a merits test to get legal aid.
claims.note: The Civil Legal Aid (Merits Criteria) Regulations set merits criteria an individual must meet to qualify.

claims.claim: The merits test considers the case's chances of success.
claims.quote: An individual may qualify for full representation only if the Director is satisfied that the criteria in regulation 39 (standard criteria for determinations for legal representation) and the following criteria are met
claims.note: A prospects of success criterion (reg. 43) applies to full representation, but the regulations do not apply it to other forms of legal aid such as legal help.

claims.claim: The merits test considers whether the case is proportionate to its cost.
claims.quote: there is likely to be sufficient benefit to the individual, having regard to all the circumstances of the case, including the circumstances of the individual, to justify the cost of provision of legal help.
claims.note: The criteria require the benefit to justify the cost, with cost benefit and proportionality tests for full representation.
